- **Reopened.** The runtime authoring surface, [issue #223](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/223). Every slice from A1 to F landed, and then a re-review of the whole run against `0bb854e` found four things that did not land with them. The first is a defect and is closed by the slice below. The other three are a duplicate reverse-topology derivation in `dependantsOf`, a quadratic `#snapshot` on the authoring side that none of the seven tick-side optimisations reached, and one unverified premise behind the empty flush seed on a removal. This file said the issue was closed with nothing open in it while the issue was open, and on the first finding the file was what was wrong rather than the state.
- **Just landed.** The immediate-verb refusal, at every verb that has one rather than at four of six. ADR-064 refuses a verb that applies immediately from inside a recipe, and `#refuseInsideRecipe` was asked by tier 0 and tier 2 alone; everything else was handled by narrowing `SchemaTransaction`. A narrowing says what a recipe is handed and cannot say what it can reach, because the recipe closes over the `ProjectHandle` its caller called `edit` on, so `seek`, `mount`, `unmount`, `invalidate` and `signal` were all reachable, none of them consulted the open transaction, and every one of them publishes or mounts immediately and survives an abort. All five refuse by name now, through the same guard and the same rule id. `#mountNode` becomes the one owner of attaching a member, because the settle step mounted through the public verb and stayed outside its guard only by the ordering of the `finally` in `edit`, and `signal` moves from a closure over the engine's Motion map onto `ProjectRuntimeOptions.signalMotion`, because the owner of the rule cannot be asked from inside that closure. `RA-79` through `RA-85` are its evidence and the amendment in [ADR-064](./ADR-064-schema-transaction-derived-hooks.md) records it.
- **The decision worth carrying forward from it.** A narrowed surface handed to a callback is not a fence. The caller still holds what it was narrowed from, so an invariant enforced by narrowing is enforced nowhere, and the refusal belongs at every verb with the shape rather than at the object the callback is given. Deferring the five instead was refused a second time, on a reason the original decision did not need: `mount` answers with the instance, `seek` and `invalidate` answer with the `PatchBatch` the caller reads, and `signal` refuses an unknown motion id, so a deferred call would answer with a batch describing a publication that has not happened. `unmount` is the one of the five that could have been deferred honestly, and deferring one of five is the two-contracts defect this closes.
- **The second one, about what was deliberately left reachable.** `subscribe` and `get`, because a listener is the caller's own object and a read of the last published patch is truthful inside a recipe. `adopt` and `destroyAdopted`, because they are structural and compose into the one commit exactly as `addTrack` does, which is what proves the narrowing was never a fence. `dispose`, because teardown has to be reachable from a `catch`. A host clock ticked from inside a recipe still publishes, and that is out of reach rather than allowed: the clock is not ours to refuse.
- **Found by that slice and not in it.** `dispose` inside a recipe clears the open transaction and empties the retained tracks, so the pair comparison in `edit` then differs and `#apply` runs against a disposed runtime, throwing from the liveness check after its effects have been applied. A disposed runtime has nothing to commit to, so `edit` should skip the apply. That is a different invariant from a refusal, so it ships on its own with its own case.

## Amendment, 2026-09-02: the narrowing was never the enforcement

One sentence of the decision above is wrong about the run, and it is the one saying that `mount`, `seek`, `subscribe` and `dispose` "are not reachable through it". They are not members of `SchemaTransaction`, which is all a narrowing can say. A recipe closes over the `ProjectHandle` its caller called `edit` on, so the same caller reaches every one of them from inside the recipe, and `#refuseInsideRecipe` was asked by tier 0 and tier 2 alone.

`seek`, `mount`, `unmount`, `invalidate` and `signal` all publish or mount immediately and survive an abort, which is the shape `schema-transaction-immediate` exists for, so all five refuse by name now. The refusal, the rule id and the mechanism are unchanged. What changes is who asks.

Deferring them was refused a second time, on a reason the original decision did not need. `mount` answers with the instance, `seek` and `invalidate` answer with the `PatchBatch` the caller reads, and `signal` refuses an unknown motion id, so a deferred call would have to answer with a batch describing a publication that has not happened, which is one boolean meaning two incompatible things one level up. `unmount` is the single member of the five that could be deferred honestly, and deferring one of five is the two-failure-contracts defect this amendment closes.

Two consequences. `#mountNode` becomes the one owner of attaching a member, because the settle step mounted through the public verb and stayed outside its guard only by the ordering of the `finally` in `edit`, and an internal caller kept out of a public refusal by the ordering of a `finally` in another method is not a thing to leave standing. And `signal` moves onto `ProjectRuntimeOptions.signalMotion`, beside `replaceMotionTrigger` and `setMotionStagger`, because it lived in a closure over the engine's Motion map where the owner of this rule cannot be asked; the unknown-motion refusal stays in that layer verbatim, and `createHandle` loses the parameter that carried it.

`subscribe`, `get`, `adopt`, `destroyAdopted` and `dispose` stay reachable, each for its own reason. A listener is the caller's own object and taken inside a recipe it receives the commit's flush. A read of the last published patch is truthful while a recipe is open, because nothing has published. The two structural verbs compose into the one commit exactly as `addTrack` does, which is what shows the narrowing was documentation rather than a fence. Teardown has to be reachable from a `catch`. And a host clock ticked from inside a recipe still publishes, which is out of reach rather than allowed: this slice refuses what the handle can reach.

Evidence `RA-79` through `RA-85` in `packages/core/test/unit/runtime/immediate-verb-refusal.test.ts`, with the accepting direction asserted in the same rig for every refusal.
